chunks: It is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “We deal with some people from the rural districts and others. We sell to them and profit from them, such that ten becomes twelve and ten becomes thirteen. We defer that between us and them for a year or about that. Then a man writes it for us against his house or against his land for that amount of money in which there is the excess, which he took from us as a purchase, on the basis that he has sold it and taken the price. Then we promise him that if he brings the money at a time agreed between us and him, we will return the purchase to him. But if the time comes upon us and he does not bring us the dirhams, then it is ours. So what do you think regarding the purchase?”
He said: “I hold that it is yours if he does not do so; but if he brings the money at the appointed time, then you must return it to him.”

key_terms.أَرْضِهِ: his land used as security in the transaction
key_terms.أَهْلِ السَّوَادِ: the people of the rural cultivated lands
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: the payment money to be brought within the term
key_terms.السَّنَةَ: the specified deferred period of a year
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: the added excess over the original amount
key_terms.دَارِهِ: his house used as security in the transaction
key_terms.نَرْبَحُ: we make a profit in sale

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a conditional sale of land or a house when payment is deferred and the seller may reclaim it within a fixed term?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a deferred sale secured by a house or land, with an agreed condition allowing the seller to reclaim the property if payment is brought within a specified term. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that the property belongs to the buyer if the seller fails to pay within the agreed time, but if he pays on time, it must be returned to him. The narration is significant in Shia fiqh for questions of conditional sale, pledged property, and contractual financial dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3770 - It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Yasar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (as):
"We deal with some people from the rural areas and others. We sell to them and make a profit - sometimes ten becomes twelve, and sometimes ten becomes thirteen. We allow them to defer payment for a year or so, and they provide us with a written guarantee secured by their house or land for the amount, including the added profit.
We then agree that if they bring the payment within the specified time, we will cancel the sale and return the property to them. However, if the deadline passes and they do not bring the payment, the property becomes ours.
What do you think about this transaction?"
Imam (as) said: "I see that it is yours if they fail to meet the condition. But if they bring the payment within the agreed time, you must return the property to them."
